headline: A student engineer who likes problems with *real inputs.*
intro: I study Information Science and Engineering at RV Institute of Technology and Management in Bangalore. I enjoy building practical applications that solve real problems: picking one, choosing the smallest stack that can solve it, and then debugging my way to something that works end to end.

My work sits where software engineering meets data. On one side are the things that make a product usable — APIs, databases, a clear interface. On the other are the models and statistics that make it useful — detection, regression, anomaly scoring, recommendation. I like projects that need both.
aspiration: I’m looking for internships in software engineering, machine learning or data science, where I can work on production systems with engineers who will push me to write better code.

approach.title: Start from the signal
approach.body: Before choosing a model I look at what the data actually is: a webcam frame, a CSV of minute-level wattage, a user’s first five picks. The shape of the input decides the design.

approach.title: Ship the whole loop
approach.body: A model in a notebook isn’t a product. I try to carry each idea through to an interface someone can use — a dashboard, an alert, a page.

approach.title: Be honest about the gaps
approach.body: Every case study on this site lists what isn’t built yet. Knowing the limits of a system is part of engineering it.

learningNext: Proper multi-object tracking (DeepSORT / ByteTrack) and evaluating it on recorded footage
LLM-backed features with real evaluation, building on my GenAI and Agentic AI coursework
Cloud deployment and CI/CD in practice — moving from AWS and Azure fundamentals to running services

interests.title: Cricket — bowling
interests.body: I bowl for the RVITM cricket team. We finished runners-up in the VTU South Zone tournament in both 2023 and 2024. Bowling is a lesson in consistency: the same line and length, over after over, adjusting a little each ball based on what the batter does.

interests.title: Building to learn
interests.body: I like experimenting with new ideas by building them: a hackathon system for crowd safety, an app that explains where an electricity bill goes, a recommender designed for users it knows nothing about yet.

interests.title: AI, closely followed
interests.body: I keep up with applied AI through structured courses — IBM, Microsoft and LinkedIn, an Agentic AI fellowship — and by trying ideas in code rather than only reading about them.
